note: SP-3000 model. Provenance tags: M=measured D=documented I=inferred G=guessed. NO measured SP-3000 data was obtainable (web fetch of most sources failed; searches found no Fuji spectral data). Most values are I/G.

sensor.note: Status M densitometry as sensor proxy (Gaussian approximations, not the ISO tables). Real SP-3000 = LED illumination + area CCD (Fuji SP500 spec page documents LED + area CCD with pixel shift; SP-3000 same family, I). Peak/FWHM provenance G, confidence low.

density.note: D=-log10(T_ch) where T_ch=integral(Tfilm*S_ch)/integral(S_ch) (equal-energy weighting; LED*CCD already inside S_ch). Scanner raw 12-16 bit, ADC clip at Tmin_floor. D-min removal: subtract per-channel D of unexposed rebate/base, I.
density.dmin_source: film rebate (unexposed area) or stock default from simulator's base transmittance

film_type_setup.note: Per-stock setup: per-channel linear map applied to Dn: D'_c = slope_c*Dn_c + offset_c, chosen so the stock's grey-card scale is neutral at mid-scale. Real Frontier film-type tables are believed to be LUT-based per channel (could be neutral along whole scale), but this is I/G. Simulator: fit slope/offset by least squares over grey ramp (e.g. zones III-VII); slope_G=1 reference.
film_type_setup.fit: least squares over grey ramp, anchored so D'_c(mid grey)=D_ref (0.75 above Dmin, G for 18% grey)
film_type_setup.neutralise: whole scale to first order (linear), curvature residual left to the film

autosetup.note: Per-frame correction algorithm. Fuji does not document it; structure is generic LATD-style (large-area transmission density, as in Fuji printers) plus highlight/shadow limits. All numbers G.
algorithm: 1 downsample to ~64x64, mask 8% border and pixels with Dn>Dn_p99.5 or <Dn_p0.5
2 LATD_c = mean(Dn_c) over masked frame (trimmed 10-90 pct)
3 density shift: dD_c = k_col*(LATD_ref_c - LATD_c) , applied additively per channel
4 grey-world: LATD_ref_c is film-setup mean of a typical frame; keeps channel difference, so colour cast partly removed
6 clamps: |dD_c|<=clamp; highlight point = percentile p_hi of positive luminance mapped to 0.95 white if headroom allows, strength k_hl
7 shadow point percentile p_lo mapped to black via the curve toe, strength k_sh
autosetup.strength_note: Strength 0-1 slider scales k_den and k_col together. Keep k_hl,k_sh at 0 by default (highlight/shadow handling is inferred only).

gradation.note: Normalised density x=(Dn_ref_white - D')/range, i.e. positive-sense log exposure scaled so x=0 black, 1 white. Output y=curve(x). Parametric: sigmoid-with-gamma: y = S(x) with toe/shoulder. Frontier look: moderately contrasty, firm blacks, soft highlight shoulder (inferred from user reports, not measured).
gradation.form: y = x_c^g blended: y = 1/(1+exp(-a*(x-m))) rescaled to [0,1], a=contrast, m=midpoint; then highlight shoulder y=y for y<ys, else ys+(1-ys)*(1-exp(-(y-ys)/(1-ys)*sh))/(1-exp(-sh))
gradation.output_encoding: y is display-referred, apply sRGB OETF-like encoding already baked in (curve is to encoded values)

colour.note: Post-curve colour. Frontier output reportedly vivid, slightly warm, strong reds/greens (user reports, G). Apply in linearised-or-encoded RGB as stated.
colour.saturation_method: scale chroma about Rec709 luma in encoded RGB

user_controls.note: Real Frontier operators have Density, C/M/Y colour keys, Contrast (gamma) and Saturation(colour), with integer key steps, commonly +/-; exact step unit unverified. Mapping below is I/G.
user_controls.sign_convention: positive Density key darkens print? unverified; use app convention: +Density = lighter image
